title: RSA identity modulo the prime $q$
statement: Let $q$ be a prime, and let $e, d, k, m, p$ be natural numbers satisfying $ed = 1 + k(p-1)(q-1)$. Then $m^{ed} \equiv m \pmod{q}$; that is, the images of $m^{ed}$ and $m$ agree in $\bbz/q\bbz$.
hypotheses_covered: e, d, k, m, p are natural numbers
replaced:
If $q$ is prime and $ed = 1 + k(p-1)(q-1)$, then $m^{ed} \equiv m$ in $\bbz/q\bbz$ for every
$m \in \bbn$.
